text:
COURT OF APPEAL FOR BRITISH COLUMBIA

Shavluk v. Green Party of Canada,

[
1
]

LOW J.A.
: This is
an appeal of an order dismissing an action brought against the Green Party of
Canada and its national leader, Elizabeth May. The appellant claimed that he
was libelled in a press release issued by the Green Party and in a conference
-call interview of Ms. May by the Canadian Jewish Political Affairs Committee. The
press release was issued on 4 September 2008; a federal election was called on
7 September; and the interview was on 16 September. The sole purpose of the
press release was to announce the removal of the appellant as a Green Party
candidate in a Greater Vancouver federal parliamentary riding. The interview
covered a number of topics, including cancellation of the appellant’s candidacy.

[
2
]

The appellant also pleaded that the respondents
had committed the tort of civil conspiracy to do him harm.

[
3
]

Following a seven-day trial, Madam Justice Ross
dismissed the action. Her reasons can be found at
2010 BCSC 804
.

[
4
]

The removal of the appellant as a candidate for
the party stemmed from discovery of a website posting made by the appellant
almost two years earlier, on 4 November 2006, and developing media interest in
the posting shortly before the federal election was called. The posting was on
an internet forum known as “Frost Cloud”. The topic of the discussion was
changing the marihuana laws. Although the text of the posting was written in
vague terms, I discern that it was mainly an attack on law enforcement by
police authorities in the United States. The posting includes the following
passage:

if we want to talk about laws,,why don’t you
care that your country started an illegal war in Iraq,,arrest some one you law
racists!!!!

everyone knows but you guys whats going to
happen and its way over due

hey i heard some guy in Australia knows
someone who says he had something to do with your governments complicate attack
on your shoddily built Jewish world bank headquarters. you know “the 2 towers”
(who has the ring i wonder)better invade there too eh,,oh no oil?

half your country’s income squandered on the
military every year and you have children going to bed hungry every night
disgusting!

the real truth about who did what and why
will come out trust me.

[
5
]

This posting by the appellant caused an obvious
political problem for the party and its leader that was intensified by current
media enquiries. There was evidence that a story about the posting was about to
appear soon in a national newspaper.

[
6
]

The Green Party’s press release reads:

John Shavluk will not be a Green candidate

4 September 2008 - 5:20pm

NEW GLASGOW – The Green Party has announced
that John Shavluk will not be the candidate for the party in Newton–North
Delta, following revelations that he made comments in 2006 on an online
discussion forum that could be construed as anti-Semitic.

“Respect for diversity is a fundamental
principle of the Green Party,” said leader Elizabeth May. “We condemn
anti-Semitism and our members work to encourage respectful dialogue, diversity,
peace and cooperation.”

“I communicated
with John and thanked him for his work on behalf of the Green Party but
explained that he will not be a candidate because his views are not consistent
with our philosophy. I will not sign his nomination papers and the Green Party
will nominate another candidate.”

[
7
]

There is some confusion in the evidentiary
record about two previous versions of this press release that were drafted and
posted electronically either generally or on a Green Party intranet site. It is
impossible for the court to resolve the confusion. In both earlier versions,
the words “could be construed as anti-Semitic” appear as “are anti-Semitic”. In
the one version, the words “I communicated with” appear as “I spoke with”. One
of these versions was still posted as late as the date of trial without having
been removed.

[
8
]

This confusion cannot form the basis of a
palpable and overriding error with respect to the evidence and the findings of
fact. Nor can it affect the outcome of any of the issues relating to the
successful defences advanced by the respondents. This is so for two reasons.
First, the claim of defamation was pleaded solely on the press release
reproduced in para. 6 above. Neither of the earlier drafts of the press release
could therefore form the basis for a finding of defamation. In any event, the
imputed defamatory sting found by the trial judge would be exactly the same.

[
9
]

Second, neither of the earlier drafts of the
press release could affect the finding of the absence of malice made by the
trial judge. It is apparent from the reasons for judgment that the Green Party
had a valid concern about the 2006 blog posted by the appellant and that it had
acted in good faith to address its effect on the appellant’s political
candidacy in a measured way (see paras. 87 and 89 of the trial judge’s
reasons). In my opinion, nothing turns on sequence, the content or the posting
of the earlier drafts with respect to any of the issues, including the issue of
malice.

[
10
]

The portion of the interview with Ms. May to
which the appellant objected is reproduced as follows:

I would be very grateful for an opportunity
to say that I know and I apologize for the fact that John Shavluk initially
passed screening. We had not seen his blog mentioning unacceptable statements.

Our Party has a
range of members, probably as big a tent as any Party out there. We believe in
free speech but we draw the line, just as we were discussing this call, on
things that are hate filled and we will never allow that to contaminate our
dialogues.

[
11
]

The trial judge found that the imputation of the
words in the press release and the interview were defamatory of the appellant
and the defence of justification failed, as did the defence of fair comment.

[
12
]

The judge also found, however, that the defences
of qualified privilege and of responsible communication on a matter of public
interest had both been made out. She further found that there was no proof of
the tort of civil conspiracy. She dismissed the action with costs.

[
13
]

The appellant contends that the trial judge
erred: (1) in finding that the defence of qualified privilege applied in the
circumstances; (2) in failing to find actual malice on the part of the
defendants so as to defeat the defence of qualified privilege; (3) in finding
that the defence of responsible communication had been established by the respondents;
and (4) in dismissing the claim for damages for civil conspiracy.

[
14
]

The respondents say that the trial judge did not
err as contended by the appellant. In addition, they say that the judge did err
in rejecting the defence of justification. However, I find it unnecessary to
consider that argument raised by the respondents.

[
15
]

The appellant has identified no arguable issue
with respect to the defence of qualified privilege or the related question of
malice. Nor has he raised any arguable issue with respect to acceptance by the
trial judge of the defence of responsible communication.

[
16
]

With respect to the defence of qualified
privilege or related question of malice, the appellant has shown no
misapprehension of the evidence, overriding or palpable error in determination
of the facts, misstatement of the law, or misapplication of the law by the
trial judge. On each of these matters, I am in substantial agreement with the
reasons of the trial judge.

[
17
]

The appellant contends that the trial judge
erred in the scope she gave to the defence of responsible communication on a
matter of public interest and that subsequent appellate decisions make this
even clearer. I find it unnecessary to consider this submission because it
could not affect the outcome. Because no error is made out on the defence of
qualified privilege, the defamation claim stands properly dismissed in any
event.

[
18
]

At trial, the appellant argued a number of
factual matters that he said gave rise to an inference of conspiracy on the
part of the respondents to do him harm. The trial judge categorically rejected
the appellant’s view of the facts on this pleaded claim. The evidence clearly
supported the judge’s conclusions and the appellant has demonstrated no basis
in law for appellate interference. This claim properly failed for the reasons
given by the trial judge.

[
19
]

I would dismiss the appeal.

[
20
]

D. SMITH J.A.
: I
agree.

[
21
]

BENNETT J.A.
: I
agree.

[
22
]

LOW J.A.
: The
appeal is dismissed.

“The Honourable Mr. Justice Low”
